Description Summary: Located in the "Northwest cemetery" of Khirbat Faynan 8. Features thin plate slag and small reed-impressed tuyères identical to those of Late Bronze Age Timna Site 30 8.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): ca. 841–771 BCE (Iron II) 7.
Description Summary: Extensive field terraces containing scatters of Iron Age pottery, representing agricultural activity supporting the smelting population 9.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): Iron Age II (by pottery) 9.
Description Summary: Features 14 blackish mining waste dumps from shafts dug into the lower Umm Ishrin formation to reach the buried Burj (DLS) ore body below 9.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): Middle Bronze, LBA (1500–1432 BCE) through the Iron Age 12, 13.
Description Summary: A model mining district studied by the GMM containing 56 recorded mines 10. Features double shafts dug through the Umm Ishrin formation to exploit deeper Burj (DLS) ore 10. Mine 42 was active in the LBA 12, while WF 1422 features both Iron Age double shafts and a Roman prospection shaft 11.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): ca. 1262–1056 BCE (LBA to Iron I) 13, 14.
Description Summary: Contains 14 mines on the mountain slopes north of Wadi Dana 11. Wood from Mine 13's tailing dump dates to the Late Bronze/Iron I transition 14. WF1431 represents a small building with an enclosure 14.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): ca. 1262–1056 BCE (LBA to Iron I) 13, 14.
Description Summary: Contains 14 mines on the mountain slopes north of Wadi Dana 11. Wood from Mine 13's tailing dump dates to the Late Bronze/Iron I transition 14. WF1431 represents a small building with an enclosure 14.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): Iron Age II (reprocessing EBA slag) 15.
Description Summary: Located on a hilltop mountain pass 15. Features a 100-ton heap of slag reprocessed and remelted during the Iron Age II to extract metal inclusions, along with rock-cut cup marks for slag crushing 15.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): ca. 1373–976 BCE (LBA to end of Iron IIA) 16-18.
Description Summary: One of the largest smelting centers in the Levant, featuring dozens of slag mounds (~50,000–60,000 tons of slag) 16. Includes a 73x73m fortress, monumental buildings, a gatehouse converted to a smelting workshop (Area A), and a highly specialized refining workshop (Area F) 16.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): ca. 1192–936 BCE (Late 12th to late 10th century BCE) 13, 19.
Description Summary: Extensive unfortified smelting site on both sides of Wadi al-Jariya containing 15,000–20,000 tons of slag 19. Represents the early, unfortified phase of Iron Age smelting before the consolidation at KEN 19.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): Iron Age 20.
Description Summary: Surveyed wadi valley featuring ~50 recorded mines, at least 26 of which yielded Iron Age pottery 20. Mines consist of shafts dug into the Umm Ishrin sandstone to exploit the buried Burj (DLS) formation 20.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): Late Iron Age (not earlier than the 8th to 6th centuries BCE) 21.
Description Summary: Dense concentration of late Iron Age sites in the upper Wadi Ghuweiba 21. RAM East features a massive sandstone block fortress next to a mining complex 22. RAM West features a local dolomite tower, rooms, and a courtyard 23. Represents late Edomite plateau-fringe operations 21.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): ca. 1192–1051 BCE (Iron I-IIA smelting) 13, 24.
Description Summary: Features extensive scatters of small slag fragments on both sides of Wadi al-Ghuweiba 24. Excavation revealed an Iron Age I–IIA smelting layer underneath a later Roman-Nabataean building 24.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): Iron Age (along with Paleolithic, EBA, Roman, and modern) 23, 25.
Description Summary: The western gateway to the Faynan district 23. Surveyed sectors documented cemeteries, campsites, and several small-scale copper smelting scatters demonstrating simpler technologies than the major lowland centers 23.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): ca. 1192–1021 BCE (Iron I reuse of EBA site) 28, 29.
Description Summary: The largest Early Bronze Age copper manufactory in the Near East 28. However, it features a large eastern surface "slag mound" confirmed by archaeomagnetism and radiocarbon to date to the Iron Age I 28.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): Primarily 10th century BCE (ca. 1090–840 BCE) 30, 31.
Description Summary: The largest Iron Age cemetery in Edom (~3,450 m²) with an estimated 1,500 to 3,000 sub-surface cist graves 30. Attributed to a mobile nomadic community (Shasu) whose members were actively engaged in smelting 30.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): EBI, reused for graves in the Iron Age 32.
Description Summary: Well-preserved EBI village and metalworking site 32. Reused during the Iron Age for isolated tumuli burials, including Tomb 1 which contained eight individuals buried with Egyptian amulets 32.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): Iron Age II 33.
Description Summary: Small mining district with 24 tailing dumps 33. Shafts were dug into the local gravel to reach the buried Burj (DLS) formation 33. Probably supplied ore to Wadi Fidan's smelting sites 33.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): Early Bronze I / Chalcolithic (with likely Iron Age reuse) 34.
Description Summary: Located near Jabal Madsus, containing 20–30 refilled pit mines ("Tellerpingen") and a nearby early smelting installation 34.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): ca. 908–843 BCE (Iron IIA / 9th century BCE) 35, 36.
Description Summary: Located far from the mines 35. Features an excavated "four-room" house (BH2) containing Midianite pottery and limited smelting remains, serving as an oasis road station on the route leading to the Gulf of Aqaba 35.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): 10th c. BCE (Iron IIA, 1050–842 BCE) and 7th–6th c. BCE (Iron IIC, 791–524 BCE) 7, 38.
Description Summary: Structural remains situated on a small, prominent inselberg 37. It is unique as the only stratified site in the Edom lowlands preserving clear evidence of both 10th-century and 7th–6th-century BCE occupations 38.

Dates of Operation (Cal. BC): Iron Age (OSL dated) 39.
Description Summary: A massive mining district consisting of three fields of pit mines (JAJ-1, 2, 3) in the colluvial/alluvial deposits of the Burj (DLS) formation, associated with a geological dike 39. It served as the main ore source for Khirbat en-Nahas 39.
